title.japanese: {体|からだ}の{慣|かん}{用|よう}{句|く}

body:
## The Body as a Map of Feelings

Every language uses the body to talk about feelings and character — English has cold feet, a big mouth, and a heart of gold. Japanese does this on an unusually large scale. Anger rises in the belly, pride lifts the nose, and social connections are measured by the width of a face. Learning a few dozen of these ⟦{慣用句|かんようく}→慣用句：15890_kanyouku⟧ (idioms) will make everyday conversation, newspapers, and drama dialogue far easier to follow, and using them makes your Japanese sound natural rather than translated.

The idioms below are grouped by body part, with a literal reading where it helps the image stick. Each links to its own dictionary entry with examples.

## ⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧: Head

The head is the seat of thinking, temper, and status.

- ⟦{頭|あたま}に{来|く}る→頭に来る：30587_atamanikuru⟧ — to get angry (literally: it comes to the head)
- ⟦{頭|あたま}を{下|さ}げる→頭を下げる：26795_atamawosageru⟧ — to bow; to apologize or ask humbly
- ⟦{頭|あたま}が{固|かた}い→頭が固い：06893_atamagakatai⟧ — stubborn, inflexible (a hard head)
- ⟦{頭|あたま}が{上|あ}がらない→頭が上がらない：30819_atamagaagaranai⟧ — to be unable to hold one's head up before someone, out of debt or respect

## ⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧: Face

The face stands for one's public self and reputation.

- ⟦{顔|かお}が{広|ひろ}い→顔が広い：06887_kaogahiroi⟧ — well connected, knowing many people (a wide face)
- ⟦{顔|かお}を{出|だ}す→顔を出す：06899_kaowodasu⟧ — to show up, to put in an appearance
- ⟦{顔|かお}が{利|き}く→顔が利く：30588_kaogakiku⟧ — to have influence; to be able to pull strings

## ⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧: Eyes

- ⟦{目|め}がない→目がない：30820_meganai⟧ — to have a weakness for something (⟦{甘|あま}い→甘い：00617_amai⟧もの⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{目|め}がない→目がない：30820_meganai⟧ — to love sweets)
- ⟦{目|め}を{通|とお}す→目を通す：06904_mewotoosu⟧ — to look through, to skim
- ⟦{目|め}が{回|まわ}る→目が回る：19927_megamawaru⟧ — to be dizzy; to be frantically busy
- ⟦{目|め}を{丸|まる}くする→目を丸くする：07448_mewomarukusuru⟧ — to be wide-eyed with surprise
- ⟦{目|め}が{離|はな}せない→目が離せない：06890_megahanasenai⟧ — to be unable to take one's eyes off something

## ⟦{耳|みみ}→耳：01513_mimi⟧: Ears

- ⟦{耳|みみ}が{痛|いた}い→耳が痛い：06892_mimigaitai⟧ — (criticism) hits home (the ears hurt)
- ⟦{耳|みみ}を{傾|かたむ}ける→耳を傾ける：06903_mimiwokatamukeru⟧ — to lend an ear, to listen carefully
- ⟦{耳|みみ}にする→耳にする：17115_miminisuru⟧ — to happen to hear
- ⟦{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}い→耳が遠い：30777_mimigatooi⟧ — hard of hearing

## ⟦{鼻|はな}→鼻：02164_hana⟧: Nose

- ⟦{鼻|はな}が{高|たか}い→鼻が高い：10096_hanagatakai⟧ — proud (a high nose)
- ⟦{鼻|はな}で{笑|わら}う→鼻で笑う：07449_hanadewarau⟧ — to sneer, to laugh through the nose

## ⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧: Mouth

Most mouth idioms are about talking — how much, how carelessly, and to whom.

- ⟦{口|くち}が{堅|かた}い→口が堅い：06885_kuchigakatai⟧ — tight-lipped, discreet
- ⟦{口|くち}が{軽|かる}い→口が軽い：06884_kuchigakarui⟧ — loose-lipped, unable to keep a secret
- ⟦{口|くち}が{滑|すべ}る→口が滑る：30585_kuchigasuberu⟧ — to let something slip
- ⟦{口|くち}が{悪|わる}い→口が悪い：30586_kuchigawarui⟧ — sharp-tongued
- ⟦{口|くち}を{挟|はさ}む→口を挟む：15229_kuchiwohasamu⟧ — to butt into a conversation
- ⟦{口|くち}に{合|あ}う→口に合う：30821_kuchiniau⟧ — (food) to suit one's taste

## ⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧: Teeth

- ⟦{歯|は}が{立|た}たない→歯が立たない：30822_hagatatanai⟧ — to be no match for; too hard to handle (the teeth cannot bite it)
- ⟦{歯|は}を{食|く}いしばる→歯を食いしばる：21568_hawokuishibaru⟧ — to grit one's teeth and endure

## ⟦{首|くび}→首：00792_kubi⟧: Neck

- ⟦{首|くび}になる→首になる：30823_kubininaru⟧ — to be fired
- ⟦{首|くび}を{長|なが}くする→首を長くする：30824_kubiwonagakusuru⟧ — to wait eagerly (stretching the neck to look)
- ⟦{首|くび}を{縦|たて}に{振|ふ}る→首を縦に振る：15468_kubiwotatenifuru⟧ — to nod yes, to agree
- ⟦{首|くび}を{横|よこ}に{振|ふ}る→首を横に振る：19743_kubiwoyokonifuru⟧ — to shake one's head, to refuse

## ⟦{肩|かた}→肩：02192_kata⟧: Shoulders

Shoulders carry burdens and take sides.

- ⟦{肩|かた}を{持|も}つ→肩を持つ：30825_katawomotsu⟧ — to side with, to take someone's part
- ⟦{肩|かた}の{荷|に}が{下|お}りる→肩の荷が下りる：30826_katanonigaoriru⟧ — to feel a weight lifted from one's shoulders
- ⟦{肩|かた}を{並|なら}べる→肩を並べる：18128_katawonaraberu⟧ — to stand shoulder to shoulder, to be on a par with
- ⟦{肩身|かたみ}が{狭|せま}い→肩身が狭い：06891_katamigasemai⟧ — to feel small, to feel out of place

## ⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧: Chest

The chest holds emotion — what English puts in the heart.

- ⟦{胸|むね}を{張|は}る→胸を張る：06900_munewoharu⟧ — to be proud, to hold one's head high
- ⟦{胸|むね}が{痛|いた}む→胸が痛む：25565_munegaitamu⟧ — to feel heartache
- ⟦{胸|むね}がいっぱい→胸がいっぱい：30827_munegaippai⟧ — to be overcome with emotion (the chest is full)

## ⟦{腹|はら}→腹：02165_hara⟧: Belly

The belly is the seat of anger and of one's true intentions.

- ⟦{腹|はら}が{立|た}つ→腹が立つ：06886_haragatatsu⟧ — to get angry (the belly rises)
- ⟦{腹|はら}を{立|た}てる→腹を立てる：30828_harawotateru⟧ — to lose one's temper, to take offense
- ⟦{腹|はら}を{割|わ}る→腹を割る：10092_harawowaru⟧ — to speak frankly, to open up
- ⟦{腹|はら}{八分目|はちぶんめ}→腹八分目：08318_harahachibunme⟧ — eating until eighty percent full
- ⟦{腹黒|はらぐろ}い→腹黒い：07740_haraguroi⟧ — scheming, black-hearted

## ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧: Hands

⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧ means both "hand" and "arm," and its idioms cover work, help, and effort.

- ⟦{手|て}を{貸|か}す→手を貸す：22775_tewokasu⟧ — to lend a hand
- ⟦{手|て}が{足|た}りない→手が足りない：30591_tegatarinai⟧ — to be short-handed
- ⟦{手|て}を{抜|ぬ}く→手を抜く：06905_tewonuku⟧ — to cut corners
- ⟦{手|て}が{空|あ}く→手が空く：30590_tegaaku⟧ — to become free, to have a moment
- ⟦{手|て}が{離|はな}せない→手が離せない：06889_tegahanasenai⟧ — to be tied up, unable to leave what one is doing
- ⟦{手|て}を{焼|や}く→手を焼く：07438_tewoyaku⟧ — to have trouble with, to find someone a handful
- ⟦{手|て}に{負|お}えない→手に負えない：15444_tenioenai⟧ — beyond one's control
- ⟦{手|て}に{入|い}れる→手に入れる：30829_teniireru⟧ — to obtain, to get hold of
- ⟦{手|て}がかかる→手がかかる：30830_tegakakaru⟧ — to require a lot of care or effort

## ⟦{腕|うで}→腕：01006_ude⟧: Arms

In idioms the arm means skill.

- ⟦{腕|うで}を{磨|みが}く→腕を磨く：07453_udewomigaku⟧ — to hone one's skills
- ⟦{腕|うで}を{振|ふ}るう→腕を振るう：07452_udewofuruu⟧ — to show off one's skill (often in cooking)
- ⟦{腕前|うでまえ}→腕前：07299_udemae⟧ — skill, ability (a noun built on the same image)

## ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧: Legs and Feet

- ⟦{足|あし}を{引|ひ}っ{張|ぱ}る→足を引っ張る：06906_ashiwohipparu⟧ — to hold someone back, to drag someone down
- ⟦{足|あし}が{出|で}る→足が出る：06888_ashigaderu⟧ — to go over budget (the legs stick out of the blanket)
- ⟦{足|あし}を{運|はこ}ぶ→足を運ぶ：06898_ashiwohakobu⟧ — to go somewhere in person, to make the trip
- ⟦{足|あし}を{洗|あら}う→足を洗う：30831_ashiwoarau⟧ — to wash one's hands of, to quit a bad line of work

## ⟦{腰|こし}→腰：02210_koshi⟧: Hips and Lower Back

- ⟦{腰|こし}が{低|ひく}い→腰が低い：06894_koshigahikui⟧ — humble, unassuming (low hips, as in a deep bow)
- ⟦{腰|こし}を{据|す}える→腰を据える：06901_koshiwosueru⟧ — to settle down to a task, to commit seriously

## ⟦{舌|した}→舌：02154_shita⟧, ⟦{喉|のど}→喉：00977_nodo⟧, ⟦{骨|ほね}→骨：02166_hone⟧: Tongue, Throat, Bones

- ⟦{舌|した}を{巻|ま}く→舌を巻く：07437_shitawomaku⟧ — to be amazed, to marvel
- ⟦{喉|のど}から{手|て}が{出|で}る→喉から手が出る：30832_nodokarategaderu⟧ — to want something desperately (a hand reaches out of the throat)
- ⟦{骨|ほね}を{折|お}る→骨を折る：17002_honewooru⟧ — to take pains, to go to great trouble for someone
- ⟦{骨|ほね}が{折|お}れる→骨が折れる：30833_honegaoreru⟧ — to be hard work, to be laborious

## How to Use Them

These idioms are ordinary phrases grammatically, so the verb or adjective at the end conjugates as usual: ⟦{腹|はら}→腹：02165_hara⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{立|た}った→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧ (I got angry), ⟦{腹|はら}→腹：02165_hara⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てている→立てる：01196_tateru⟧ (is angry), ⟦{目|め}が{回|まわ}る→目が回る：19927_megamawaru⟧ほど⟦{忙|いそが}しい→忙しい：00591_isogashii⟧ (busy enough to make your head spin). They can also modify nouns: ⟦{顔|かお}が{広|ひろ}い→顔が広い：06887_kaogahiroi⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (a well-connected person), ⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{堅|かた}い→堅い：18753_katai⟧⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧ (a discreet friend).

The particle is part of the idiom and cannot be changed, and neither can the words: ⟦{腹|はら}が{立|た}つ→腹が立つ：06886_haragatatsu⟧ does not become ⟦お{腹|なか}→お腹：00805_onaka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧, and ⟦{顔|かお}が{広|ひろ}い→顔が広い：06887_kaogahiroi⟧ does not become ⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大|おお}きい→大きい：00335_ookii⟧. Many of these phrases also keep their literal meaning — ⟦{目|め}が{回|まわ}る→目が回る：19927_megamawaru⟧ can describe real dizziness, and ⟦{手|て}が{離|はな}せない→手が離せない：06889_tegahanasenai⟧ can mean your hands are literally full — so let the context decide.

## Tips for Learners

1. **Learn the image, not just the translation.** "The belly rises," "the nose is high," and "a hand reaches out of the throat" are easier to remember than abstract glosses, and they make the meaning transparent.
2. **Keep the particle attached.** Memorize ⟦{肩|かた}を{持|も}つ→肩を持つ：30825_katawomotsu⟧ as one unit; ⟦{肩|かた}→肩：02192_kata⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧ means nothing.
3. **Start with the ones you will meet daily.** ⟦{顔|かお}を{出|だ}す→顔を出す：06899_kaowodasu⟧, ⟦{手|て}が{離|はな}せない→手が離せない：06889_tegahanasenai⟧, ⟦{口|くち}に{合|あ}う→口に合う：30821_kuchiniau⟧, ⟦{腹|はら}が{立|た}つ→腹が立つ：06886_haragatatsu⟧, and ⟦{首|くび}になる→首になる：30823_kubininaru⟧ appear constantly in conversation and drama.
4. **Notice the cultural map.** Anger and honesty live in the belly, pride in the nose and chest, and reputation in the face. Once you see the pattern, unfamiliar idioms become guessable.
5. **Follow the links.** Every idiom above has an entry with example sentences and notes on register.
